meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'german', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: You promised to talk with German.

examples.text: И с Германом я уже поговорил вчера.
examples.trans: And I already spoke with German yesterday.
And what did German say to you?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hands', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Денис, откуда у тебя в руках живой голубь?
examples.trans: Denis, where did you get a live pigeon in your hands?

examples.text: Так, друзья, где мой голубь по-дижонски?
examples.trans: All right, folks, where is my Dijon squab?

examples.text: Откуда под крышкой взялся этот живой голубь?
examples.trans: Where did that live pigeon under the cover come from?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'restaurant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Разве в нашем ресторане гости едят голубей?
examples.trans: Do guests really eat pigeons in our restaurant?

examples.text: Нет, только не трогай этих дорогих голубей!
examples.trans: No, just do not touch those expensive pigeons!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, отдай мне хотя бы одного голубя!
examples.trans: Please give me back at least one pigeon!

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

meanings.en: debtor, someone who owes money or books
meanings.note: Animate masculine noun. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'debtor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Because you are a chronic debtor.
The bank phoned all the debtors.

examples.text: Я вообще вам могу ничего не давать! Потому что вы злостный должник.
examples.trans: I don't have to give you anything at all! Because you are a chronic debtor.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('living, alive, live').

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'bake', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Сеня, ты что творишь, предатель несчастный?

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to fix, to correct, to put right
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, to correct', paired with 'исправлять'.

examples.trans: Excuse us, we will fix everything.

examples.text: Ученик быстро исправил ошибку в тетради.
examples.trans: The pupil quickly corrected the mistake in his notebook.

examples.text: Да, вы знаете, это очень серьёзная операция. Мы всё исправим. До свидания!
examples.trans: Yes, you know, it is a very serious operation. We'll fix everything. Goodbye!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'acid', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'partridge'.

examples.text: Куропатка оставалась, а выбрасывать было жалко.
examples.trans: Partridge was left over, and it was a shame to throw it out.

examples.text: Нет, Федя сам жарил эту куропатку!
examples.trans: No, Fedya roasted that partridge himself!

meanings.note: Impersonal predicate or adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It's easy for you to say.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

meanings.note: подать подписи = to submit signatures
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to submit, file; to serve', paired with 'подавать'.

examples.text: Ирина Петровна, скажите, пожалуйста. Кандидат Самсонов подал подписи с нарушениями, ведь да?
examples.trans: Irina Petrovna, tell me, please. Candidate Samsonov submitted his signatures with violations, isn't that right?

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun in -тель. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'атель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'traitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего я тебе не скажу, предатель!
examples.trans: I won't tell you anything, traitor!
The traitor revealed the secret to the enemy.

examples.text: Это ведь вопрос воспитания. Кого может воспитать предатель?
examples.trans: It is a question of upbringing, after all. Whom can a traitor raise?

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

продумать.gloss: to think through, to plan out

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think through, to plan out', paired with 'продумывать'.

examples.text: В Москву. Я уже всё продумала.
examples.trans: To Moscow. I've already thought everything through.

meanings.note: a warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrate distinguished by feathers

examples.trans: Birds have a very weak heart.

examples.text: Что нужно сделать с этой птицей?
examples.trans: What needs to be done with this bird?

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ахар'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sugar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Очень плохой кофе. Девочка, дай сахар, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Very bad coffee. Girl, pass me the sugar, please.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прятать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hide', paired with 'прятать'.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.

meanings.note: Hot liquid dish. Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Tableware. Common feminine noun meaning 'plate, platter, dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.
Put clean plates on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: colloquial: что вы творите? = what are you doing?
Elevated. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to perpetrate; to create', paired with 'сотворить'.

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!
softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
